title.narrative: Investing for impact against Tuberculosis and HIV - Nigeria (01-Jul-2015-31-Dec-2018)

description.narrative: Nigeria, the most populous African nation, ranks 4th among the high tuberculosis (TB) burden countries in the world, according to the 2009 WHO Global TB Report, and first in Africa with an estimated 460,000 new cases annually. TB constitutes a considerable public health problem: in 2007, the national TB Program reported 2,189 TB patient deaths. The TB burden is borne by the entire population, but especially by higher risk populations, such as the urban and rural poor, people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) and those in congregate settings including prison inmates, armed forces personnel, and socially marginalized and displaced persons. There is also a significant socio-economic consequence of TB in Nigeria, as the disease is most prevalent among the most economically productive age range of 15-45 years. In 2010 the WHO estimates, that there were an estimated 11,000 (95% C.I. 1,300-20,000) MDR-TB cases in Nigeria in 2008, based on expected incidence. This corresponds to an estimated MDR-TB rate of 1.8% (95% C.I. 0.0-4.3) among new cases and 7.7% (95% C.I. 0.0-18.1) among retreatment cases. However based on notified pulmonary TB cases in 2009 the best estimate of MDR cases are 1,900 (95% C.I. 600 – 3,900). This Program aims to reduce the TB burden by complementing and accelerating the ongoing activities implemented by government, partners, including USAID, and through the Global Fund Round 5 program (NGA-509-G15-T). In particular, the focus of this Program is to strengthening the MDR TB program implementation. This Program implements the remaining components of the Round 9 TB proposal. That proposal was designed to be “split” into two grants to be implemented by two principal recipients. The DOTS expansion and TB/HIV component was signed in September 2010 with the Association for Reproductive and Family Health (ARFH). The second part of the proposal with the MDR-TB component was not signed due to challenges associated with identifying a principal recipient that met minimum capacity requirements. The CCM nominated one principal recipient in mid-2009 which underwent LFA assessments but which regrettably did not meet minimum requirements. The CCM subsequently launched an open and transparent procedure, based on Global Fund policies, to identify a new principal recipient. Based on this process, the CCM nominated the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN) as the Principal Recipient and on 15 December 2010, IHVN was selected as Principal Recipient for this Grant. On 26 March 2010, The Technical Review Panel approved the MDR-TB component of the proposal for a patient cohort of 80 patients (Initial MDR-TB Approval). The CCM with assistance of the WHO TB Team and the Green Light Committee, has also prepared a reprogramming request to the Technical Review Panel of the Global Fund (TRP) to support scale-up and required health system strengthening (HSS) of the MDR-TB program to address previous TRP concerns raised during the TRP clarification process. The TRP has approved the reprogramming request on 23 June 2011 (Scale Up). The Global Fund Board approved a 3 month extension to the signing deadline for this Grant until 20 May 2011 (B22/ER/02). This Grant will also be signed as a SSF grant, fully aligned with the Round 9 TB grant with ARFH (DOTS and TB/HIV).
